trait.description: The uniformity of the plant

method.description: Observe the uniformity of the plant and rate it

categories: 1 = Very heterogeneous (Height, vigor, growth stage very heterogeneous.)
3 = Heterogeneous (75% of the plants show height, vigor and growth stage heterogeneity.)
5 = Intermediate (50% of the plants show height, vigor and growth stage heterogeneity)
7 = Uniform (75% of the plants show height, vigor and growth stage homogeneity)
9 = Very uniform (100% of the plants show height, vigor, growth stage homogeneity)

trait.description: The vigor of the plant

method.description: Observe the vigor of the plant and rate it

categories: 1 = Very weak (All the plants are small (< 20 cm), few leaves, weak plants, very thin stems and/or light green color)
3 = Weak 95% of the plants are small (< 20 cm) or all the plants are between 20 and 30 cm, the plants have few leaves, thin stems and/or light green color)
7 = Vigorous (75% of the plants are over 50 cm, robust with foliage of dark green color, thick stems and leaves very well developed)
9 = Very vigorous (All the plants are over 70 cm and ground coverage is complete. The plants are robust, with thick stems and abundant foliage of dark green color)

trait.description: The senescence of the plant

method.description: Observe the senescence of the plant and rate it

categories: 1 = Very late (All the plants still show green foliage and flowers)
3 = Late (Most of the plants are still green, flowering is over and berries might be formed)

5 = Medium (the plants are still being green or on the onset of senescence, there may be a slight yellowing. The angle of insertion of the leaves on the stems may have become more obtuse than in the younger plants of the same clone. The formation of berries can be advanced and abundant in fertile clones)
7 = Early (The plants have senescent foliage, yellowing is more advanced but the stems may still be upright. If berries are present, their color will turn from green to pale green or yellow green.)
9 = Very early (The plants are completely senescent, yellowing is complete and uniform, and the stems are decumbent)

trait.description: The wilting of the canopy

method.description: Observe the Degree of canopy wilting and rate it

categories: 1=No wilting (All the plants still show green foliage and turgid)
3=Slight (Most of the plants are still green and turgid, 25 % plants with in the plot show slight wilting evidence by leaf dropping (wilting) and rolling in the bottom of the canopy)
5=Medium (50 % of the plants show leaf rolling in the bottom of the canopy, moderate wilting of leaves throughout the canopy and some loss of petiole turgidity)
7=Severe (75% of the plants show wilt: the petioles severely wilted and dry leaves in the bottom of the canopy)
9=Very severe (100% of the plants show very severe water stress: completely wilted plant and dry leaf)
